18.body: Fuse supports standard SQL with datasource.table addressing for cross-datasource queries.
18.title: SQL Reference

19.body:
SELECT service, status, message
FROM cluster_a.application_logs
LIMIT 10 Table names use datasource_id.table_name format. The datasource ID comes from your fuse.toml config.
19.title: SELECT

2.body: Same-type federation — Query across multiple OpenSearch clusters with UNION ALL Cross-type federation — JOIN OpenSearch data with S3 or Prometheus SQL + PPL — Full support for both query languages Query pushdown — Filters, projections, and limits pushed to connectors Data provenance — _datasource column shows where each row came from Execution profiling — EXPLAIN and ANALYZE with visual plan tree 5 connectors — OpenSearch, S3 Parquet, S3 O11y (NDJSON), Prometheus, custom via SDK Caching — TTL-based query result cache per connector type Alerting — Rule-based alerting on federated queries Materialized views — Pre-computed cross-datasource views
2.title: Key Features

20.body:
SELECT service, message
FROM cluster_a.application_logs
WHERE status >= 500 AND service = 'api-gateway'
LIMIT 20 Filters are pushed down to connectors when supported.
20.title: WHERE

21.body:
SELECT service, count(*) as errors, avg(response_time_ms) as avg_ms
FROM cluster_a.application_logs
WHERE status >= 500
GROUP BY service
ORDER BY errors DESC Supported functions: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX.
21.title: GROUP BY + Aggregations

22.body:
SELECT service, response_time_ms
FROM cluster_a.application_logs
ORDER BY response_time_ms DESC
LIMIT 10
22.title: ORDER BY + LIMIT

23.body:
Combine results from multiple datasources: SELECT service, status, message
FROM cluster_a.application_logs
UNION ALL
SELECT service, status, message
FROM cluster_b.application_logs
LIMIT 20 Cross-cluster queries add a _datasource column automatically. See Data Provenance .
23.title: UNION ALL (Cross-Cluster)

24.body:
Join data across different datasource types: SELECT l.trace_id, l.service, l.status, s.level, s.message
FROM cluster_a.application_logs l
JOIN s3_o11y.fuse_logs s ON l.trace_id = s.trace_id
WHERE l.status >= 500 Fuse uses hash-join for cross-datasource JOINs. Both sides are fetched in parallel, then joined locally.
24.title: JOIN (Cross-Datasource)

25.body:
SELECT service, cnt
FROM ( SELECT service, count(*) as cnt FROM cluster_a.application_logs GROUP BY service
) sub
WHERE cnt > 10
ORDER BY cnt DESC
25.title: Subqueries

26.body: Always use LIMIT to avoid fetching entire indices Use WHERE clauses — they get pushed down to connectors for performance SELECT * works but explicit column lists enable projection pushdown Check the EXPLAIN / ANALYZE page to understand query plans
26.title: Tips

27.body: Piped Processing Language (PPL) uses a pipe syntax: source = datasource.table | command | command.
27.title: PPL Reference

29.body: Specify one or more datasources: source = cluster_a.application_logs Multi-source (cross-cluster): source = cluster_a.application_logs, cluster_b.application_logs

3.body:
# Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/seraphjiang/fuse.git
cd fuse
cargo build --release # Run with sample config
./target/release/fuse-server --config fuse.toml # Query
curl -X POST http://localhost:9400/api/fuse/query \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"query": "SELECT * FROM cluster_a.application_logs LIMIT 5"}'
3.title: Quick Start

30.body:
Filter rows: source = cluster_a.application_logs
| where status >= 500
| where service = 'api-gateway'
| head 20
30.title: where

31.body:
Aggregate with optional grouping: source = cluster_a.application_logs
| stats count() as total by service
| sort - total Functions: count(), sum(), avg(), min(), max().
31.title: stats

32.body:
Sort results. Use - for descending: source = cluster_a.application_logs
| sort - response_time_ms
| head 10
32.title: sort

33.body: Limit output rows: source = cluster_a.application_logs | head 5
33.title: head

34.body:
Select specific fields: source = cluster_a.application_logs
| fields service, status, message
| head 10
34.title: fields

35.body:
Remove duplicate rows by field: source = cluster_a.application_logs
| dedup trace_id
| head 10
35.title: dedup

36.body:
Create computed fields: source = cluster_a.application_logs
| eval is_error = status >= 500
| where is_error = true
| head 10
36.title: eval

37.body:
Query across clusters in a single PPL statement: source = cluster_a.application_logs, cluster_b.application_logs
| where status >= 500
| stats count() as errors by service
| sort - errors
| head 10 This fans out to both clusters, merges results, then applies the pipeline.
37.title: Multi-Source Queries

38.body: PPL commands are applied in order (left to right through pipes) where pushes down to connectors when possible Use head to limit results early Multi-source queries add a _datasource column — see Data Provenance
38.title: Tips

6.title: Prerequisites

60.body: Fuse ships with 5 connectors. Each implements the FederatedConnector trait and is registered via a ConnectorFactory.
60.title: Connectors

61.body:
The primary connector. Supports OpenSearch and Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (AOSS). [[connector]]
id = "cluster_a"
connector_type = "opensearch"
endpoint = "https://abc123.us-west-2.aoss.amazonaws.com"
auth = "sigv4"
region = "us-west-2" Auth options: none, basic, sigv4 For basic auth: auth = "basic"
username = "admin"
password = "admin" Capabilities: filtering, projection, aggregation, sorting, limit, streaming. Pushdown: WHERE clauses become Query DSL filters. SELECT columns become _source includes. LIMIT becomes size.
61.title: OpenSearch

62.body:
Read Parquet files from S3. [[connector]]
id = "data_lake"
connector_type = "s3"
bucket = "my-data-bucket"
prefix = "warehouse/"
region = "us-west-2" Auth: IAM (uses default credential chain). Capabilities: filtering, projection, limit.
62.title: S3 Parquet

63.body:
Read gzipped newline-delimited JSON from S3. Designed for observability log pipelines. [[connector]]
id = "s3_o11y"
connector_type = "s3-o11y"
bucket = "s3-query-logs-544277935543-us-west-1"
prefix = "fuse/"
region = "us-west-1" Auth: IAM. Format: Gzipped NDJSON files at {prefix}{YYYY/MM/DD/HH}/{timestamp}.json.gz. Schema discovery: Automatic from first file. Fields: any JSON keys found in records.
63.title: S3 O11y (NDJSON)

id = "metrics"
connector_type = "prometheus"
endpoint = "https://prometheus.example.com"
auth = "bearer"
token = "your-token" Auth options: none, bearer Capabilities: filtering (time range), projection.

66.body: When a query touches multiple datasources, Fuse adds a _datasource column to every row indicating which datasource produced it.
66.title: Data Provenance

67.body:
For cross-datasource queries (UNION ALL, multi-source PPL, JOINs), each row gets tagged: SELECT _datasource, service, status
FROM cluster_a.application_logs
UNION ALL
SELECT _datasource, service, status
FROM cluster_b.application_logs
LIMIT 10 Result: _datasource service status cluster_a api-gateway 500 cluster_a auth-service 200 cluster_b order-service 500 cluster_b payment-service 200
67.title: The _datasource Column

68.body:
The response metadata includes per-datasource statistics: { "metadata": { "datasources_queried": ["cluster_a", "cluster_b"], "datasource_stats": { "cluster_a": { "rows": 12, "latency_ms": 45 }, "cluster_b": { "rows": 8, "latency_ms": 67 } } }
} In the playground UI, this appears as a color-coded provenance bar below the results table.
68.title: Datasource Stats

69.body: Use LIMIT — Cross-cluster queries can return large result sets. Always limit. Filter early — WHERE clauses push down to each connector, reducing data transfer. Check provenance — Use _datasource to verify data is coming from expected sources. Monitor latency — datasource_stats shows which connector is slow. A slow connector delays the entire query. Use EXPLAIN — Check the execution plan to verify pushdown is working.
69.title: Cross-Cluster Best Practices
